message.content:
Technicians don’t come to *me*—they’re part of the customer companies. When a drone crashes or has a fault, it’s their job to check the logs, fix it, and get it back in the air.

I only see the drone’s location and status if it’s still in the airspace system. If it’s grounded, it’s out of my picture. Sometimes a drone just disappears from the system, and that’s when the companies have to figure out what happened. They usually call me if a closure or site issue might have caused the problem, but mostly it’s their fault logs and their people who know.
